qt: to the Commission Ioan-Rareş Bogdan (PPE) Subject:

While I welcome the Commission’s commitment to tackling migrant smuggling networks in the Mediterranean region under the Pact for the Mediterranean, I note that the updated action plan includes the launch of the ‘Secure Borders’ initiative, which is supposed to bolster the institutional and border management capabilities of partner countries in the Southern Neighbourhood. Yet Romania and the other eastern flank Member States are spending huge sums to manage and guard thousands of kilometres of the Union’s external border that are under direct pressure from hybrid threats and the ongoing regional conflict. I therefore ask the Commission: 1.
What is the total financial envelope that has been allocated to the ‘Secure Borders’ initiative to support border authorities in North Africa, and from which instruments does this funding come?

On the basis of what criteria is the Commission prioritising allocating non-reimbursable funds to equip the border agencies of non-EU countries over using the general budget to fully cover the costs of guarding the external borders of exposed Eastern Member States?

How much direct and non-repayable Union funding was allocated in the last financial year to security infrastructure along the Romanian section of the external border, and how do these figures compare with the sums provided to Southern Neighbourhood states?
